quickAnswer: At Turkish airports, standard liquids, aerosols, and gels in cabin baggage are capped at 100ml per container inside one transparent 1-liter bag. Post-op shampoos, foams, and large saline bottles belong in checked luggage, while essential liquid medications over 100ml require original packaging plus a signed prescription or medical report naming the passenger.

body.text: Flying home from Istanbul or Antalya after a procedure requires a different packing approach than a routine holiday. Security rules enforced by Türkiye's [Directorate General of Civil Aviation (SHGM)](https://web.shgm.gov.tr/tr/s/5219-sivi-kisitlamalari-uygulamasi) and [iGA Istanbul Airport](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/departing-passenger-guide/services/complimentary-services/security-and-baggage-restrictions?locale=en) apply to both domestic and international departures. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders help clients organize departure logistics ahead of time so airport screening stays calm and predictable. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
Which post-op shampoos, foams and saline sprays exceed 100ml and must be checked?

Most post-procedure wash kits distributed by clinics—including 150ml or 200ml panthenol foams, 250ml mild medical shampoos, antiseptic washes, and full-size isotonic saline cans—exceed the 100ml cabin limit. Under [Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs air passenger rules](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/havayolu-yolcu-tasimaciligi.en.mfa), any non-exempt liquid, gel, cream, or spray over 100ml must travel in checked hold luggage.

Security officers evaluate the printed capacity on the bottle, not how much product remains inside. A half-empty 150ml saline mist or 120ml scar gel tube will still be confiscated at the airside X-ray belt. Before you leave your hotel, inspect every bottle in your discharge bag and separate anything cosmetic or hygienic over 100ml into your checked suitcase, wrapped in zip-top bags to prevent cabin-pressure leaks.

body.text: What prescription letters allow essential liquid meds in carry-on?

Under [iGA Istanbul Airport security guidelines](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/departing-passenger-guide/services/complimentary-services/security-and-baggage-restrictions?locale=en), essential liquid or gel medications over 100ml are exempt from standard volume limits only when kept in their original packaging and accompanied by a signed prescription or medical report bearing the passenger's full name and the prescribed drug name.

If you have a connecting flight through Europe or the United Kingdom, you will pass security screening again at your transfer hub. Both the [European Commission aviation security policy](https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/air/aviation-security/aviation-security-policy/liquids-aerosols-and-gels_en) and the [UK Civil Aviation Authority](https://www.caa.co.uk/air-passengers/about-your-trip/health-and-medical/travelling-with-medicines-mobility-and-medical-equipment/) recognize medical exemptions for liquids required during the journey, provided you carry supporting documentation in English. Ask your treating clinic during discharge—not at the airport—for a stamped English medical letter listing each liquid medication, dosage, and clinical necessity, and confirm any injectable or syringe rules directly with your airline before departure.
How do you pack ice packs or cooling gels safely?

Standard gel-filled ice packs count as gels under airport liquid rules and are frequently confiscated in carry-on if they exceed 100ml or begin thawing into a soft liquid state. The safest way to carry reusable gel packs is inside checked baggage, while cabin cooling should rely on empty zip bags that flight attendants can fill with ice onboard.

If your doctor specifically instructs you to keep a temperature-sensitive medication chilled during the flight, request a written note stating that the cooling pack is medically required for that drug, and verify airline approval in advance. Avoid loose chemical cold packs in carry-on unless clearly labeled and medically documented, as security agents can reject unverified gel pouches during secondary screening.
What should stay in your personal under-seat bag?

Your personal under-seat bag should hold every solid prescription tablet, original blister pack, medical report, fit-to-fly certificate, and small <=100ml comfort item you would need if your checked suitcase were delayed. Keeping essential medications out of checked baggage prevents missed doses during baggage delays or tight layovers.
Use this departure checklist the evening before your flight:

items: Solid prescriptions in original boxes: Antibiotics, pain relievers, anti-swelling tablets, and blood-thinning regimens prescribed by your doctor.
Stamped English documentation: Discharge summary, prescription copies, and medical letter for any liquid medication over 100ml.
One transparent 1-liter bag: Travel-sized saline spray (<=100ml), lip balm, eye drops, and small antibiotic cream tubes.
Comfort and hygiene spares: Clean gauze pads, neck pillow, empty reusable water bottle (fill after security), and spare compression socks if advised by your clinician.
Contact card: Printed hotel, airline, and clinic emergency numbers in case your phone battery dies.

faq.q: Can I bring a 150ml saline spray in my cabin bag from Istanbul Airport?
faq.a: No, unless you have a signed medical report or prescription specifically requiring that bottle during the flight. Standard 150ml saline sprays are treated as non-exempt aerosols and must go in checked luggage.

faq.q: Do liquid restrictions apply at the Istanbul Airport terminal entrance?
faq.a: No. According to iGA Istanbul Airport, liquid limits are enforced at the main airside security checkpoint after check-in, not at the initial terminal entrance X-ray.

faq.q: Can I decant post-op clinic shampoo into a 100ml travel bottle?
faq.a: Yes, for non-prescription washes or shampoos, decanting up to 100ml into a clean travel bottle inside your 1-liter pouch is allowed. Keep prescription medications in their original pharmacy packaging.

faq.q: Will European transfer airports honor a Turkish clinic's medical letter?
faq.a: Transfer checkpoints in the EU and UK generally accept clear English medical letters and original pharmacy labels for medically necessary liquids, though security staff may run additional swab or X-ray screening.

faq.q: Are pills and capsules subject to the 100ml liquid rule?
faq.a: No. Solid tablets, capsules, and dry bandages are not counted as liquids, though keeping them in original labeled boxes with your prescription prevents customs or security delays.

faq.q: Should I pack extra doses in my under-seat bag?
faq.a: Yes. Pack enough doses to cover your flight plus a 48-hour buffer in case of flight cancellations or delayed checked baggage, following your doctor's dosing instructions.
